status: DEVELOPMENT / NON-CANON / REPRODUCIBLE MEASUREMENT OF EXISTING SVG

source.map_draft: World-Atlas-Draft-V1.md sections 11-13 and coordinate framework V0.5

coordinate_transform.interpretation: The SVG uses a linear longitude/latitude plotting scaffold equivalent to an equirectangular (Plate Carrée) coordinate layout. It is not an equal-area projection.

method.surface: Unit sphere; area fractions do not depend on chosen sphere radius.
method.edge_interpretation: Each straight SVG polygon edge is treated as linear interpolation in longitude and latitude between its endpoint coordinates.
method.area_integral: For each edge, integrate sin(latitude) d(longitude) analytically; take the absolute signed spherical polygon area, selecting the smaller region.
method.formula: A = abs(sum over edges of delta_lambda * (cos(phi_start) - cos(phi_end)) / (phi_end - phi_start)); for a horizontal edge use delta_lambda * sin(phi_start).
limitations: This measures the existing V0.5 polygon paths under the stated linear lon/lat edge interpretation; it does not validate whether those paths are the desired final coastlines.
No cartographic projection beyond the SVG coordinate scaffold is asserted as the production map projection.
No plate containment, plate-motion, tectonic, climate, relief, or hydrology validation is included.
The Earth-like radius is used only to express illustrative area in km2; area fractions are radius-independent.
The six-continent fraction is the sum of the six mapped polygons only; islands and any additional land are not included.

decision.retain_old_planar_targets_as: historical design targets only; do not label them measured spherical land shares
decision.current_geographic_status: V0.5 remains a coordinate scaffold and six-continent concept, not a final geographic atlas
next_steps: Decide whether the spherical measured shares or the old 15/18/24/13/9/21 targets should guide revised coastlines.
If the 30% land assumption is retained, revise continent geometry or explicitly reserve additional land for islands/other landmasses.
Define the globe orientation and plate rotation, then test each continent polygon against its assigned carrier-plate spherical face.
Only after containment and area targets pass, proceed to relief, hydrology, climate, and biomes.
